findings.title: Register one app; customers connect via OAuth code flow
findings.detail: Register the app once in the Developer Console to get client_id/client_secret and exact redirect URIs. Customers must not register their own apps. Each customer signs in at dropbox.com to authorize, the app exchanges the code at /oauth2/token, and a user-scoped access token is returned. A server-side web app can use the code flow with the client_secret kept secure; PKCE is for clients that cannot keep a secret.

steps.title: Register one Dropbox app in the Developer Console
steps.detail: Developer registers a single app in the Dropbox Developer Console (https://www.dropbox.com/developers). Choose scoped access with the App Folder content access option. Do not have customers register their own apps. Collect the app key (client_id) and app secret (client_secret) from the app Settings tab. Store the secret in a server-side secret manager, never in client code or logs.
steps.doneWhen: The app exists in the Developer Console with App Folder access selected, and client_id and client_secret are stored in a secret manager.

* **App Folder:** Your application will be able to take actions allowed by its scopes on data within its app folder *only* (in the /apps folder). This option is suitable

steps.title: Select only the files.metadata.read scope
steps.detail: In the app Permissions tab select only files.metadata.read, which list_folder and list_folder/continue require. Do not select write scopes, content read scopes, sharing scopes or team scopes. This covers metadata-only listing and respects the prohibitions on downloading, modifying and team administration. App Folder access limits actions to the app's /apps folder. Requesting more than needed may deter customers and affect review.

steps.title: Register exact redirect URIs and prepare the callback
steps.detail: In the app Settings tab, OAuth 2 section, add the exact redirect URI(s) under Redirect URIs. Dropbox checks the redirect_uri in the authorization URL against registered values at authorization time. Agent can prepare a server-side HTTPS callback route that: reads code and state from the query string, verifies state against the value stored in the user's session, and never logs the code. Generate a random state per authorization attempt. This is a server-side app that can keep client_secret, so PKCE is not required.
steps.doneWhen: The exact callback URL is listed under Redirect URIs and the callback route exists and rejects requests whose state does not match.

evidence.quote: * You'll need to register the exact redirect URI(s) your app may use in the Developer Console for your application. Add them under **Redirect URIs** in the OAuth 2 section
of the Settings tab. Dropbox checks that the specified `redirect_uri` parameter in your Authorization URL matches one of the registered values at authorization time.
* If your application needs additional context to complete the redirect, you may pass a `state` parameter the authorization URL - which will be returned as a query parameter in

steps.title: Send a test customer to consent and validate the callback
steps.detail: Build the authorization URL and open it as a browser GET with a representative customer Dropbox account that is not the developer account. The customer signs in at dropbox.com and approves access. Dropbox redirects to the registered redirect_uri with code and state in the query string. Validate state, then stop; do not exchange yet. The docs show client_id, redirect_uri and response_type=code as the base parameters. For offline access, add token_access_type=offline to receive a refresh_token; omit it if listing only happens during user sessions.
steps.doneWhen: The browser lands on the registered callback with a code query parameter and a state value matching the one sent.

evidence.quote: `https://www.dropbox.com/oauth2/authorize?client_id=MY_CLIENT_ID&redirect_uri=MY_REDIRECT_URI&response_type=code` 2. Wait for the end user to complete authorization on dropbox.com, whom is then redirected back to your URI with an authorization code
in the query string
**Note** : you’ll need to include `token_access_type=offline` as a parameter on your Authorization URL in order to return a `refresh_token` inside your access token payload.

steps.title: Exchange the authorization code for an access token
steps.detail: From the server only, call the /oauth2/token endpoint with the app's client_secret to exchange the code for an access token (documented in s3-p69). Standard OAuth code-flow parameters grant_type=authorization_code, code, redirect_uri (matching the one used in consent) and client credentials are not itemized in the supplied excerpts; confirm them in the Dropbox token endpoint reference before coding. Store the access token (and refresh_token if requested) encrypted, keyed to the customer; never log or expose them to the browser. Access tokens are short-lived.
steps.doneWhen: The token response contains an access_token and expiry for the test customer, and the token is stored encrypted server-side without appearing in logs.

evidence.quote: 3. Call the /oauth2/token endpoint with your app’s `client_secret` to exchange the code for an access token in order to make API calls

When using refresh tokens, your call to the /oauth2/token endpoint with the `grant_type` of `authorization_code` will return a short-lived access token and a refresh token, which should be securely stored.
When using the code flow, your app must keep the `client_secret` secure. If your app can’t guarantee it’s security, then we recommend the use of PKCE as described below

steps.title: Test token expiry, refresh and revocation
steps.detail: Confirm behavior when the token expires (401 expired_access_token) and when the customer revokes the authorization. If offline access was requested, exchange the refresh_token at /oauth2/token with grant_type=refresh_token and confirm a new short-lived token is returned. Otherwise re-run the consent flow, which needs no input if the customer is signed in and approval is still valid. Verify the app handles the failure by prompting reconnection.
steps.doneWhen: An expired token is replaced via refresh or re-authorization, and a revoked authorization produces a reconnect prompt rather than a crash.

To update your access token, call the /oauth2/token endpoint - specifying your `refresh_token` as a parameter and using the `grant_type` of `refresh_token`. The endpoint will return a new short-lived access
Your application may then securely store the token for future use. Authorizations may be revoked by the user, whereas apps may revoke tokens they receive.
